source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Leviticus 23–25. The exact original XML records include all five source annotations, including the written not and read has a wall at 25:30; no numbering shift occurs in this batch.

key_decisions.decision: Retains volunteer growth and untended vine categories; note distinguishes organized harvesting from permitted eating in the following verses.
Preserves the full beneficiary list and explicitly names both sexes of enslaved people rather than hiding them within servants.
Retains both date and named day, both soundings, and the explicit shofar absent from 23:24.
Preserves fifty, all-inhabitant proclamation, Jubilee and both returns; does not erase later restrictions on the persons released.
Retains the difficult sixth/eighth/ninth-year sequence as written rather than adjusting it to an assumed calendar.
Preserves divine ownership and both ger and toshav labels for Israel, connecting land tenure with resident status rather than absolute ownership.
Follows the explicit read form has a wall over written not; preserves permanent tenure, descendants and the Jubilee exception.
Keeps redeem from the Levites as a provisional reading of the difficult opening, notes alternatives, and does not silently insert a negative absent from the pinned text.
Unfolds failing-hand idiom and selects resident-like support for the brother; note preserves possible inclusion of foreigners as additional beneficiaries.
Keeps both Hebrew financial terms and the brother’s continuing livelihood, without narrowing the ban to excessive rates.
Preserves the sale and the specific ban on slave labor rather than making the transaction ordinary voluntary employment.
Retains both comparison statuses and the Jubilee endpoint without adding modern contract terms.
Retains the source’s ownership metaphor using slaves in both halves so the exodus-based contrast remains visible; vocabulary explains the broader eved range.
Keeps the ban on harsh mastery and direct divine motivation without inventing a prohibition beyond the stated group.
Preserves explicit purchase of both sexes from surrounding nations and its repetition, rather than euphemizing slavery as service.
Preserves children of residents, families born in the land and property status; does not turn residence into a guarantee against enslavement.
Retains inheritance, permanent enslavement and the explicit Israelite limitation of the harsh-rule prohibition, without smoothing away the unequal treatment.
Keeps changed economic positions and all purchaser categories; member is provisional for the rare eqer, with descendant/offshoot noted.
Preserves annual hired-worker comparison and the addressed community’s witnessing responsibility implied by before your eyes.
Preserves both statements of divine ownership and the exodus ground with the same slave term as verse 42.
